impact_map: Incorrect scope enforcement could expose one agent's authority or evidence to another.
Collapsed provider or lifecycle state could cause a model or host to treat discoverability as activation.
Mutable or non-idempotent receipts could corrupt the evidence chain under replay.
Stale session facts could preserve expired permissions, authentication, catalog, or health claims.
A second writer or damaged migration could corrupt the Core metadata authority.
Parser or dispatcher ambiguity could permit oversized input, duplicate-key confusion, or mutation through the query surface.
Availability misclassification could report an unreadable owner store as authoritatively empty.

invariants.statement: Mutable operational facts and their evidence remain inside one exact agent/session scope.
Capability identity, provider, distribution, lifecycle, invocation, fitness, and health remain distinct; no active bit is derived.
Receipts and receipt edges are append-only, scope-compatible, acyclic, idempotent within scope, and bound to the exact typed record they evidence.
A child observation cannot outlive its host session, and an expired session makes its dependent facts stale.
Exactly one process owns the Core writer lease for a database at a time.
Phase 1 records metadata and answers queries without claiming automatic delivery, activation, interception, or dispatch control.
AUTHORITATIVE_EMPTY requires a successful authoritative read through an open, valid owner runtime.

risks.statement: When scoped records cite or expose another agent's receipts, authority and operational truth can leak across agents.
When names or global lifecycle facts collapse providers and operational axes, a caller can infer a capability is active without evidence.
When receipts replay, mutate, form cross-scope ancestry, or evidence an unrelated same-scope record, evidence can duplicate, diverge, disclose provenance, or support false operational truth.
When child facts outlive their host session, expired catalog, permission, authentication, and health claims can appear current.
When migration integrity or writer exclusion fails, the sole Core metadata authority can corrupt or fork.
When framed input is ambiguous or query dispatch is open-ended, malformed data or a mutation route can cross the H0 boundary.
When availability enum membership is accepted without semantic guards, an unreadable owner store can be reported as authoritatively empty.
When Core boot requires Nova or optional providers, MIND ceases to be a persona-neutral portable base.
When the declared build backend is unavailable, source behavior may be verified while the distributable package remains unproved.

scenarios.title: Cross-agent receipt, lifecycle, mount, and catalog access is denied
preconditions: Two agent instances have distinct host sessions and scoped receipts.
action: Use Agent A evidence from Agent B, use an unrelated same-scope receipt, and query each agent's scoped state.
expected: Cross-scope evidence is not found, unrelated same-scope evidence fails typed binding, and Agent B catalog contains no Agent A observation.
forbidden: Creating, linking, or returning Agent A scoped evidence through Agent B, or using an irrelevant receipt as operational evidence.

scenarios.title: Provider and lifecycle truth remains factored
preconditions: The public-safe bootstrap fixture is ingested.
action: Resolve EGDOD and MIND by exact handle or alias.
expected: EGDOD is canonical-constructed and not-generated with no distribution; MIND has two distinct provider distributions; derived_active_state is null.
forbidden: Installed, invoked, healthy, or merged-provider state inferred from identity records.

scenarios.title: Receipt replay, typed binding, and ancestry preserve one immutable evidence chain
action: Replay identical and changed keys, bind lifecycle/mount/grant records, substitute unrelated receipts, add same/cross-scope parents, attempt mutation and a cycle.
expected: Exact replay returns one receipt; target type, ID, and payload must match; changed replay, irrelevant evidence, incompatible ancestry, mutation, deletion, duplicate edges, and cycles fail.
forbidden: Duplicate receipt effect, changed content under one key, irrelevant evidence substitution, or cross-scope parent disclosure.

scenarios.title: Session expiry bounds dependent facts
preconditions: A host session and its catalog snapshot are expired.
action: Read session freshness and scoped observations.
expected: Session, catalog, permission, authentication, grants, lifecycle, and mount observations cannot be rendered fresh after parent expiry.
forbidden: A child timestamp reviving expired host authority.

scenarios.title: Store startup, restart, migration custody, and writer exclusion fail closed
preconditions: An isolated SQLite path is available.
action: Open competing same-process and child-process writers, tamper migration checksum, supply corrupt bytes, then close and reopen clean state.
expected: Competing writers, tampered schema, and corrupt bytes are rejected; clean close releases the lock and bootstrap state survives restart.
forbidden: Second writer admission, silent migration acceptance, partial metadata loss, or an unreleased clean-close lock.

scenarios.title: Bounded framing and explicit query allowlist preserve H0
preconditions: A fresh Core and in-memory binary streams exist.
action: Round-trip Unicode through complete and short-reading streams; send truncated, oversized, duplicate-key, and non-standard-number frames; submit a type-confused parameter; request a mutation-like method.
expected: Complete valid frames survive short reads; malformed and type-confused inputs fail; mutation method is not found; query response declares H0.
forbidden: Ambiguous parse, backend-dependent framing, dynamic dispatch, silent truncation, or an H1-H3 claim.

scenarios.title: Availability states require semantically compatible evidence
preconditions: A known-unregistered Dunbar mount and scoped observation receipt exist.
action: Record a path-visible runtime-closed result; substitute an unrelated same-scope receipt; bind a grant; and attempt AUTHORITATIVE_EMPTY without a successful read or with reported-only evidence.
expected: The first state is BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE; unrelated receipts, unbound grants, unproved emptiness, and reported-only emptiness are rejected.
forbidden: Treating path visibility, receipt scope alone, runtime failure, or weak evidence as authoritative emptiness.

scenarios.title: Core boots persona-free without optional providers
preconditions: No Nova, TestForge, Obsidian, Dunbar runtime, continuity runtime, or Mnemosyne provider is configured in the Core database.
expected: Core opens, persona_required and persona_inference are false, and maximum conformance is H0.
forbidden: Synthetic persona assignment or import-time optional-provider dependency.

scenarios.title: PEP 517 package build requires the declared backend
preconditions: Python 3.14 and pip are present; no dependency installation is authorized.
action: Probe the declared setuptools build backend before attempting a wheel build.
expected: The missing backend is recorded as an environment limitation and no package-build claim is made.
forbidden: Installing an undeclared dependency automatically or reporting an unbuilt wheel as verified.

findings.statement: Initial receipt consumers checked evidence existence but not scope compatibility, permitting cross-agent provenance.
findings.next_action: Retain the centralized scope validator, SQL scope guard, and negative regression tests.

findings.statement: Initial repeat handshakes regenerated immutable agent creation time and rejected every later session for the same agent.
findings.next_action: Preserve create-once agent identity and immutable persona/profile tests.

findings.statement: The first EGDOD oracle matched forbidden words inside an explicit non-claim boundary instead of inspecting typed lifecycle states.
findings.next_action: Keep the corrected typed axis/state assertion.

findings.statement: The heuristic smell scan flagged the identifier catalog_snapshot as a snapshot assertion in helper data and a freshness assertion.
findings.next_action: Treat these three matches as reviewed false positives; do not rename the protocol field to appease a heuristic.

findings.statement: The first reviewed revision enforced receipt scope but allowed an unrelated same-scope receipt to evidence lifecycle and mount truth.
findings.next_action: Retain exact receipt-type, subject-kind, target-ID, canonical-payload, scope, and strong-empty-evidence checks; require independent re-review.

findings.statement: The first reviewed revision treated a short read from a complete BinaryIO frame as truncation.
findings.next_action: Retain exact-read accumulation plus strict duplicate-key, non-standard-number, nesting, and parameter-type rejection tests.

findings.statement: The local Python environment lacks setuptools, so a PEP 517 wheel build was not executed.
findings.next_action: Run an isolated no-network build with the declared backend before package or release qualification; do not install dependencies implicitly in this task.

findings.statement: The first recorded aggregate target digest omitted its path set and byte-framing contract; the first repair then hashed checkout-dependent working-tree bytes instead of canonical Git blobs.
findings.next_action: Require every reviewed aggregate digest to ship its canonical content source, exact ordered path set, per-file sizes and hashes, framing algorithm, and an independent recomputation receipt.
